newsitem.title: CANADA: Summit acquires U.S. oil and gas interests.
newsitem.headline: Summit acquires U.S. oil and gas interests.

text.p: Canada's Summit Resources Ltd said on Tuesday it acquired stakes in three new oil and gas projects in the United States.
In North Dakota, Summit bought a 50-percent interest in 83,000 acres in the Ordovician Red River "B" petroleum fairway being developed using horizontal drilling technology, it said.
The geological deposition extends over 100 miles, covering portions of the states of Montana, North Dakota and South Dakota, Summit said.
The company's lands at Crooked Creek are located in Harding County, South Dakota. Summit, as operator, plans to start evaluation drilling in early 1997, it said.

In central Montana, Summit acquired an average 85-percent working interest in 51,000 acres. Three dimensional seismic was acquired on two blocks held by Summit in the productive Tyler channel sand trend, it said.
Drilling operations and more seismic programs are planned for 1997.

Summit said it also entered the growing Cotton Valley Pinnacle reef play in the East Texas salt basin. The firm has an average 25 percent working interest in 75,000 acres located in Smith and Rusk Counties. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
